summary: This standards-track memo defines a name form called a permanent identifier, which can go in the subjectAltName extension of an X.509 certificate. A certification authority can use it to show that several certificates belong to the same entity, even if the names differ.

eli5.summary: People can change their names, but a number on their ID card stays the same. This adds such a lasting number to digital certificates.

questions: what is an x509 permanent identifier
how to link certificates to the same entity
what is the permanent identifier in subjectaltname
how to tell two certificates belong to the same entity
what is an assigner authority in a certificate
subtitle: A certificate name form that stays the same even when a person's name, job or location changes.

tldr.problem: The subject name in a certificate changes when any part of it changes, for example when someone moves to another organization unit, legally changes their name or relocates. Then it is hard to tell that two certificates belong to the same entity.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4043 defines a permanent identifier, an otherName form in the subjectAltName extension. It carries an identifier value and an optional assigner OID that names the authority and type of identifier.
tldr.outcome: Relying parties can link certificates, access control entries and audit records to one entity whatever its subject name is. The same linking can conflict with privacy, so CAs should disclose its use.

today: RFC 4043 is a Proposed Standard from May 2005. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Names Change, Entities Do Not
sections.content:
A public key certificate identifies its subject through the subject field and/or the subjectAltName extension. When the subject field is non-empty it MUST hold an X.500 distinguished name (DN), and that DN MUST be unique for each subject certified by a single CA.

The DN changes whenever any of its components changes. The RFC gives three examples: an employee moves to a different organization unit, a citizen changes name by legal process (especially through marriage), or a subject identified by location relocates and changes attributes such as country, state, locality or street.

Including such details in a name is useful to relying parties, but it means the name is a poor long-term handle for the same entity.
sections.eli5: If you find someone by their class and teacher, you lose them when they switch classes. A lasting ID number still finds them.

sections.title: What a Permanent Identifier Is For
sections.content:
A permanent identifier is an identifier value assigned within a naming space by the organization that is authoritative for that space. That organization may be the issuing CA or a different one, called an Assigner Authority (a government, an agency, a corporation or any other organization). An Assigner Authority MUST have a unique identifier, and in this standard it MUST be an object identifier (OID).

The RFC names three uses: access control (an ACL entry need not change when the subject name changes), non-repudiation (linking transactions to the same entity) and audit records (linking records to the same entity).

For two certificates that have both been verified as valid under a given validation policy, matching permanent identifiers mean they relate to the same entity, whatever the DN or other subjectAltName parts contain.
sections.eli5: Whoever hands out the number, a school or a government office, has its own unique stamp. Two cards with the same stamp and number belong to the same person.

sections.title: The PermanentIdentifier Structure
sections.content:
The identifier is defined as a form of otherName from the GeneralName structure in SubjectAltName. Its use is OPTIONAL. A CA that includes one is certifying that any certificate containing the same values refers to the same entity.

It is a SEQUENCE of two optional fields. identifierValue is a UTF8String. assigner is an OBJECT IDENTIFIER that identifies a naming space, meaning both an Assigner Authority and the type of identifier; typically the OID prefix names the authority and a suffix names the type.

If identifierValue is absent, the value of the serialNumber attribute from the deepest RDN of the subject DN is used. There MUST be at least one such attribute, otherwise the PermanentIdentifier SHALL NOT be used. If assigner is absent, the assigner is the certificate issuer and the identifier is local to that CA.

The name form's own OID is id-on-permanentIdentifier, which is { id-on 3 }, where id-on is { id-pkix 8 }.
sections.eli5: It is a small form with two blanks: the number itself and who issued it. If the number is blank, you copy the one already written on the certificate's serial number line.

sections.title: The Four Combinations and How They Match
sections.content:
Which fields are present decides how far the identifier is unique and how two identifiers are compared.

  • Both present: globally unique among all CAs. They match if the assigner fields match and the identifierValue strings consist of the same Unicode code points in the same order.
  • Only identifierValue: local to the issuing CA. They match if the issuer DNs match under the distinguishedNameMatch rule and the values have the same code points in the same order.
  • Neither present: the deepest serialNumber is used, and the identifier is local to the CA. They match if the issuer DNs match and the serialNumber attributes in the subject DNs match using caseIgnoreMatch.
  • Only assigner: the deepest serialNumber is used, and the identifier is globally unique. They match if the assigners match and the serialNumber attributes match using caseIgnoreMatch.

In the last two cases, if no RDN contains a serialNumber attribute, the definition is invalid and the identifier SHALL NOT be used.
sections.eli5: If the number comes with the name of whoever issued it, it works anywhere. If not, it only means something inside that one office.

sections.title: Security and Privacy Considerations
sections.content:
When two certificates carry identical permanent identifiers, a relying party may conclude they refer to the same entity. Without an assigner field, only certificates from the same CA can be compared. With one, certificates from different CAs can be compared, and the CA is responsible for verifying that the identifier refers to the subject being certified.

Two certificates under the same issuer DN with the same identifier and no assigner do not necessarily refer to the same entity, because a name is only unique towards its superior CA. Extra checks are needed, such as comparing the CAs' public keys or the sequence of CA names in the certification path. A CA key rollover makes this more complicated.

If a certificate contains attribute extensions, the permanent identifier should not be used for access control but only for audit, since those attributes may change.

Linking certificates may conflict with privacy. CAs SHOULD advertise to certificate purchasers that permanent identifiers are used, and should clearly disclose plans to issue them.
sections.eli5: A lasting number makes it easy to see that two cards belong to the same person, which is handy but also means someone can follow them around. So the office should tell people first.

sections.title: IANA Actions and Organization OIDs
sections.content:
No IANA actions are necessary. However, a Private Enterprise Number may be used to construct an OID for the assigner field.

Appendix B explains how an organization can obtain its own OID from a registration authority following X.660. It covers using IANA, whose private enterprise prefix is 1.3.6.1.4.1, and also an ISO Member Body or an International Code Designator from the British Standards Institution. Appendix A gives the ASN.1 module in a 1988 form, which is normative, and a 1993 form.
sections.eli5: To stamp numbers with your own name, you first need your own registered code, and the appendices explain where to get one.
